English-03.question: 2) ‘Waiting for Godot’ is ________.
English-03.exp:
Waiting for Godot, tragicomedy in two acts by Irish writer Samuel Beckett, published in 1952 in French as En attendant Godot and first produced in 1953. Waiting for Godot was a true innovation in drama and the Theatre of the Absurd first theatrical success. The play consists of conversations between Vladimir and Estragon, who are waiting for the arrival of the mysterious Godot, who continually sends word that he will appear but who never does.
Samuel Beckett, in full Samuel Barclay Beckett, (born April 13, 1906, Foxrock, County Dublin, Ireland—died December 22, 1989, Paris, France), author, critic, and playwright, winner of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1969. He wrote in both French and English and is perhaps best known for his plays, especially En attendant Godot (1952; Waiting for Godot).

English-03.question: 25) When did Lord Byron die?
English-03.exp:
Lord Byron, in full George Gordon Byron, 6th Baron Byron, (born January 22, 1788, London, England—died April 19, 1824, Missolonghi, Greece), British Romantic poet and satirist whose poetry and personality captured the imagination of Europe.
Renowned as the “gloomy egoist” of his autobiographical poem Childe Harold’s Pilgrimage (1812–18) in the 19th century, he is now more generally esteemed for the satiric realism of Don Juan.
His other poems are:
- Lara,
- The Vision of Judgment,
- Robert Southey etc.

English-03.question: 31) The poem ‘The Rape of the Lock’ was written in-
English-03.exp:
The Rape of the Lock, mock-epic poem in heroic couplets by Alexander Pope. The first version, published in 1712, consisted of two cantos; the final version, published in 1714, was expanded to five cantos. Based on an actual incident and written to reconcile the families that had been estranged by it, The Rape of the Lock recounts the story of a young woman named Belinda who has a lock of hair stolen by an ardent young man.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 48) In which style did Sir Thomas Wyatt write sonnet?
English-03.exp:
The father of the English sonnet is Sir Thomas Wyatt(1503-1542). He introduced the Italian sonnet (Petrarch's sonnets) and Theresa Reimer verse form and the French Rondou into English literature.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English-03.question: 49) Who is the writer of ‘A Christmas Carol’?
English-03.exp:

Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 50) The period from AD 1660 to 1700 is known as-
English-03.exp:
The Neo-classical period (1660-1798) is divided into three periods. Such as
1. The Restoration Period (1660-1700),
2. The Augustan Age or the Age of Pope (1700-1745) and
3. The Age of Sensibility or The Age of Johnson (1745-1798).
Source: Live MCQ lecture.

English-03.question: 52) Who translated ‘the new testament’?

English-03.question: 53) What is the meaning of Renaissance?
English-03.option1: ক) the revival of hard work
English-03.exp:
The Renaissance was a fervent period of European cultural, artistic, political and economic “rebirth” following the Middle Ages. Generally described as taking place from the 14th century to the 17th century, the Renaissance promoted the rediscovery of classical philosophy, literature and art.
Source: history.com
Renaissance is a French word meaning “rebirth.” It refers to a period in European civilization that was marked by a revival of Classical learning and wisdom.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica
A new growth of activity or interest in something, especially art, literature, or music.
Source: Cambridge Dictionary
A revival of or renewed interest in something.
Source: Oxford Dictionary

English-03.exp:
Around the World in Eighty Days is an adventure novel by the French writer Jules Verne, first published in French in 1872.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 67) Who wrote ‘Les Miserables’?
English-03.exp:
Les Misérables is a French historical novel by Victor Hugo, first published in 1862, that is considered one of the greatest novels of the 19th century.
Verified From: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 68) Goethe is the greatest poet of-
English-03.exp:
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749—1832), German poet, playwright, novelist, scientist, statesman, theatre director, critic, and amateur artist, considered the greatest German literary figure of the modern era.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 69) ‘The strongest man in the world is he who stands most alone’ was stated by-
English-03.exp:
The strongest man in the world is he who stands most alone.
Henrik Ibsen

English-03.question: 70) Who is the author of the novel ‘A Golden Age’?
English-03.exp:
A Golden Age is the first novel of the Bangladesh-born writer Tahmima Anam. It tells the story of the Bangladesh War of Independence through the eyes of one family. The novel was awarded the prize for Best First Book in the Commonwealth Writers' Prize 2008.
Verified From: Amazon, Daily Star & The Guardian.

English-03.question: 71) ‘The God of Small Things’ is written by-
English-03.exp:
In 1997 Arundhati Roy published her debut novel, The God of Small Things to wide acclaim. The semi-autobiographical work departed from the conventional plots and light prose that had been typical among best-sellers.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 72) Tolstoy was born in ______.
English-03.exp:
Leo Tolstoy (1828—1910) Russian author, a master of realistic fiction and one of the world’s greatest novelists.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 73) Who wrote the book ‘Dr. Zhivago’?
English-03.exp:
Doctor Zhivago, novel by Boris Pasternak, published in Italy in 1957. This epic tale about the effects of the Russian Revolution of 1917 and its aftermath on a bourgeois family was not published in the Soviet Union until 1987. One of the results of its publication in the West was Pasternak’s complete rejection by Soviet authorities; when he was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1958 he was compelled to decline it. The book quickly became an international best-seller.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 74) Who wrote the book ‘Cancer Ward’?
English-03.exp:
Cancer Ward is a semi-autobiographical novel by Nobel Prize-winning Russian author Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 75) What is true about Wole Soyinka?
English-03.option1: ক) He studied theatre in London.
English-03.option2: খ) He is an English playwright, British novelist.
English-03.option3: গ) He is a nigerian theatre artist.
English-03.exp:
Wole Soyinka's family belongs to the Yoruba people, whose culture has influenced his works. After studying in Nigeria and the UK, he worked at a theatre in London.
Source: nobelprize.org

English-03.question: 76) ‘Corruption wins not more than honesty’ who told it?
English-03.exp:
Corruption wins not more than honesty.
- William Shakespeare.

English-03.question: 77) ‘Good face is the best letter of recommendation’ was stated by-
English-03.exp:
A good face is the best letter of recommendation.
- Queen Elizabeth I

English-03.question: 78) ‘Power tends to corrupt and absolute power corrupts absolutely’ who said?
English-03.exp:
Power tends to corrupt and absolute power corrupts absolutely.
- Lord Acton

English-03.question: 79) Who believed that ‘poetry is the spontaneous overflow of emotions’?
English-03.exp:
William Wordsworth is a famous Romantic poet.
Famous quotes of Wordsworth:
'Child is the father of man',
'Our birth is but a sleep and a forgetting',
'Nature never did betray the heart that loved her',
'Poetry is a spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings',
'Poet is the breath and final speed of knowledge',
'Come forth into the light of things, let nature be your teacher'.
Source: Live MCQ lecture

English-03.question: 80) An epic is-
English-03.exp: Epic: a long poem, typically one derived from ancient oral tradition, narrating the deeds and adventures of heroic or legendary figures or the past history of a nation.

English-03.question: 81) Ballad means-
English-03.exp: Ballad- a slow sentimental or romantic song.

English-03.question: 82) Elegy is-
English-03.exp: Elegy: (in modern literature) a poem of serious reflection, typically a lament for the dead.

English-03.question: 83) ‘Dramatic monologue’ is used in-
English-03.exp: Dramatic monologue: a poem in the form of a speech or narrative by an imagined person, in which the speaker inadvertently reveals aspects of their character while describing a particular situation or series of events.

English-03.question: 84) What is the meaning of ‘Soliloquy’?
English-03.option4: ঘ) Long self speech by an actor
English-03.exp: Soliloquy: an act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when by oneself or regardless of any hearers, especially by a character in a play.

English-03.question: 85) Tragedy means-
English-03.option1: ক) a serious play with a happy ending
English-03.option2: খ) a serious play with a sad ending
English-03.option3: গ) a humorous play with a sad ending
English-03.option4: ঘ) a funny play with a touchy ending
English-03.exp: Tragedy: A play dealing with tragic events and having an unhappy ending, especially one concerning the downfall of the main character.

English-03.question: 86) A novel in the form of a letter is called-
English-03.exp:
Epistolary novel, a novel told through the medium of letters written by one or more of the characters. Originating with Samuel Richardson’s Pamela; or, Virtue Rewarded (1740), the story of a servant girl’s victorious struggle against her master’s attempts to seduce her, it was one of the earliest forms of novel to be developed and remained one of the most popular up to the 19th century. The epistolary novel’s reliance on subjective points of view makes it the forerunner of the modern psychological novel.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 87) Which composition emphasizes on the author's witness and experiences rather than his/her own personality or life?
English-03.exp: Memoir: a historical account or biography written from personal knowledge.

English-03.question: 88) Metaphor is a comparison between-
English-03.exp: A metaphor is a figure of speech that is used to make a comparison between two things that aren't alike but do have something in common. Unlike a simile, where two things are compared directly using like or as, a metaphor's comparison is more indirect, usually made by stating something is something else.

English-03.question: 89) ‘We have short time to stay, as you’ (from the poem ‘To Daffodils’) is an example of-
English-03.exp: যদি কোন বাক্যে দুটো জিনিসের মধ্যে তুলনা বুঝায় এবং As, like থাকে তাহলে তাকে Simile বলে। যেমনঃ The soul was like a star dwelt apart. The child shows the man, as morning shows the day.

English-03.question: 90) A climax is-
English-03.option2: খ) a point of greatest intensity
English-03.option3: গ) a crisis in a drama
English-03.option4: ঘ) the latest scene in a drama
English-03.exp:
The peak of importance in a play or story is called climax. At this point the rise of action ends and the fall of action begins. For example: Antigone’s death is the climax of Oedipus.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English-03.question: 91) ‘There is no one so poor as a wealthy miser.’ This is an example of-
English-03.exp:
Paradox, apparently self-contradictory statement, the underlying meaning of which is revealed only by careful scrutiny. The purpose of a paradox is to arrest attention and provoke fresh thought. The statement “Less is more” is an example. Francis Bacon’s saying, “The most corrected copies are commonly the least correct,” is an earlier literary example.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 92) Substitution of an unpleasant or vulgar expression is called-
English-03.exp:
Euphemism:
English Meaning: A word or phrase used to avoid saying an unpleasant or offensive word.
Bangla Meaning: সুভাষণ; সত্যিকার শব্দের পরিবর্তে অন্য কোনো শব্দের ব্যবহার- যেমন ‘মৃত্যু’ শব্দের বদলে ‘পরলোকগমন' বাক্যাংশের ব্যবহার।

English-03.question: 93) If a part of a speech or writing breaks the theme, it is called-
English-03.exp: Digression: a temporary departure from the main subject in speech or writing.

English-03.question: 94) Which one is not a literary ornament?
English-03.exp:
Similar ইংরেজি ভাষার সাধারণ একটা শব্দ, যার অর্থ সদৃশ বা একই।
অন্যান্য অপশনের শব্দ গুলো ইংরেজি সাহিত্যে বিশেষ ভাবে ব্যবহার করা হয়ে থাকে।
Simile- উপমা, দুটি ভিন্নধর্মী জিনিসের মধ্যে like অথবা as ব্যবহার করে সুস্পষ্ট তুলনা।
Similitude- সাদৃশ্য, তুলনা, উপমা।
Sarcasm- অনুভূতিকে আহত করার উদ্দেশ্যে ব্যবহৃত তিক্ত মন্তব্য এবং ঐরূপ মন্তব্যের ব্যবহার; শ্লেষ; শ্লেষোক্তি; পরিবাদ।
Source: Bangla Academy Dictionary.

English-03.question: 95) ‘For God’s sake hold your tongue, let me love.’ This line is written by-
English-03.exp:
For God's sake hold your tongue, and let me love,
Or chide my palsy, or my gout,
My five gray hairs, or ruined fortune flout,
With wealth your state, your mind with arts improve,
Take you a course, get you a place,
Observe his honor, or his grace,
Or the king's real, or his stampèd face
Contemplate; what you will, approve,
So you will let me love.
- John Donne

English-03.question: 96) ‘Death in the Afternoon’ is a non-fiction book written by-
English-03.exp:
Ernest Hemingway is an American novelist. He was awarded the Nobel prize in 1954 for literature.
His famous novels are For Whom The Bell Tolls, The Old Man and The Sea, A Farewell to Arms, The Sun Also Rises, Death in the Afternoon, To Have and Have not.
Source: Live MCQ Lecture.

English-03.question: 97) ‘Gitanjali’ of Rabindranath Tagore was translated by-
English-03.exp:
Gītāñjali is a collection of poetry, the most famous work by Rabindranath Tagore, published in India in 1910. Tagore then translated it into prose poems in English, as Gitanjali: Song Offerings, and it was published in 1912 with an introduction by William Butler Yeats.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

English-03.question: 98) Find the odd-man out-
English-03.exp: George Eliot (victorian poet & novelist) ছাড়া বাকি তিনটি অপশনের সবাই আধুনিক যুগের কবি।

English-03.question: 99) The ‘Poet Laureate’ is-
English-03.option1: ক) The best poet of the country
English-03.option2: খ) A winner of the Nobel Prize in poetry
English-03.option3: গ) The Court poet of England
English-03.exp:
Poet Laureate: An eminent poet appointed as a member of the British royal household.
Source: Oxford Dictionary.
The title of poet laureate was first granted in England in the 17th century for poetic excellence.
Source: Britannica Encyclopedia.

English-03.question: 100) The literary work ‘Kubla Khan’ is-
English-03.option1: ক) A History By Vincent Smith
English-03.option3: গ) A Drama By Oscar Wilde
English-03.option4: ঘ) A Short Story By Somerset Maugham
English-03.exp:
Kubla Khan or, a Vision in a Dream, poetic fragment (verse) by Samuel Taylor Coleridge, published in 1816.
Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.
